title: The View from Nowhere: Population-Centered Agent Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2610.36660v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-improving AI systems can revise the designs that govern their own behavior. Yet existing approaches center improvement on selected parent agents and their evolutionary experience, leaving the broader population largely underused. We identify a substantial gap between population coverage (i.e., the tasks solved by at least one evolved variant) and the performance of the best individual agent. This gap shows that useful capabilities and diagnostic evidence emerge across the population without being consolidated into its leading agents.   These observations motivate the view from nowhere, a principle for agent evolution: an agent should be improved by interpreting its behavior through population-wide patterns of success, failure, and prior self-modification. translated_title: 无处之观：以种群为中心的智能体演化
translated_abstract: 自我改进的AI系统能够修改支配其自身行为的设计。然而，现有方法将改进集中在被选中的父代智能体及其演化经验上，使得更广泛的种群在很大程度上未被充分利用。我们发现种群覆盖率（即至少被一个演化变体解决的任务）与最佳个体智能体的性能之间存在显著差距。这一差距表明，有用的能力和诊断证据在种群中广泛涌现，却未被整合进领先的智能体之中。这些观察催生了“无处之观”（the view from nowhere）这一智能体演化原则：应当通过种群范围内的成功、失败及先前自我修改的模式来解读智能体的行为，从而对其进行改进。我们将这一原则具体化为种群中心演化（Population-Centered Evolution, PCE）。PCE 将种群中的任务记录和修改历史提炼为一个种群块，该块捕获……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出种群中心演化（PCE），通过利用整个种群的任务记录与自我修改历史来改进智能体，从而弥合种群覆盖率与最佳个体性能之间的差距。
en_tdlr: Proposes Population-Centered Evolution (PCE), which improves agents by leveraging population-wide task records and self-modification histories to close the gap between population coverage and best-individual performance.
